whyChoose.title: Why Campbell Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Matter
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, prioritizing a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents. An attorney can quickly assess where you fit and what that means for your claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Waiting to get guidance can cost you options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, as well as compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help you understand the full scope of what may be available.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Campbell?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the claim involves a government entity, such as a city or county road, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier notice. Speaking with an attorney soon after a loss helps preserve your options.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California law gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to file a wrongful death claim. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Does Campbell's crash pattern near SR-17 or Hamilton Avenue affect our case?
items.answer: Public crash records show that reported collisions in Campbell tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. along corridors like SR-17, San Tomas Expressway, and Hamilton Avenue. That pattern can provide useful context, but every case depends on its own facts. An attorney can look at the specific circumstances of your loss.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may result from the same incident. The civil claim focuses on compensating the family for their losses, not on punishing the at-fault party through the criminal system. Both can proceed independently of one another.
